answer: Binding each identity to a hardware attestation resists sybils: an identity is only valid when anchored to a secure-enclave key certified as unique, so one device yields one identity. A tide of fake accounts hits a physical wall: minting a thousand identities means buying a thousand devices, not running a script. The terrace of trust rises slowly, since a new device starts with minimal weight and gains influence only through honest work, so a bought device cannot vote at full power on day one, and a device caught cheating loses its attestation for good.
